headline: Payton Tolle silences Baltimore as the Sox stay red hot
morning_brew: Payton Tolle put on a straight-up clinic in Baltimore, making those Orioles hitters look like they were swinging garden hoses. Twelve strikeouts in six innings of work is the kind of filth that makes me want to start a fan club for his changeup right now. That is the command we have been praying for all damn summer, and watching him carve up that lineup meant I didn't have to watch the game through my fingers for once. Erik Miller, Jovani Morán, and Aroldis Chapman came in after and absolutely locked the place down. It was the kind of clinical, professional showing that makes you start checking the calendar for October dates.

The bats did just enough to keep us in the driver's seat, and while we did not exactly light up the scoreboard, the efficiency was there when it mattered. It was a hell of a relief to watch our pitchers dictate the tempo for once, instead of the usual heart-attack baseball we get at Fenway. My mother actually called me after the final inning and said it felt like the team finally remembered how to play fundamental baseball without forcing her to reach for the blood pressure medication. I know the standings are tight, but playing with this much swagger in a hostile yard is exactly the shot in the arm this team needed.

We are right back at it this afternoon, and I am not looking at the standings or worrying about what the Blue Jays are doing until we finish the business in front of us. My old man always told me that you can only control the inning you are currently playing, and this squad is finally starting to act like they believe it. I will be parked in front of the TV for first pitch with a fresh Dunks, hoping to see another performance that keeps us climbing. If we keep playing like this, I might finally have to make a meaningful deposit in the Duck Boat fund.

news_digest.headline: Jaylen Brown receives key to city in farewell party to Boston
news_digest.dans_take: It is a tough one to swallow, but the city turned out to give him the proper send-off he earned.
